diagnosis: hp.v1 has 35 resolved names over 3 run days (11-06, 11-09, 11-10). Brier is 0.2492, a skill of 0.003 over a coin. Direction is 16/32 and there are 0 recommendations. The control (also hp.v1, frozen) has 12 names at Brier 0.2416. The paired difference on those 12 is -0.004 (sd 0.031, t -0.45), and because both arms ran the same text, that figure is the stage's reproducibility noise, not an effect. The views carry no information yet, and the reason is not miscalibration: every evolving p_up sits between 38 and 58, and only 3 of 35 are 10 or more points from 50. That spread is honest for a researcher with no edge. Two mechanisms in the playbook keep it there. (1) The researchers read P7's mechanism clause together with P4 and P8 as 'the deciding line must be visible before the release'. It never is, so on name after name they gathered dated evidence on the inputs to that line and then sat near 50 with 'no public trace before the release' (QBTS, HSAI, CRWV, RKLB, STUB, HIMS, LQDA). Where the inputs pointed, the facts often followed. RKLB's guide-beat record was right: record revenue, backlog +52% q/q, Q4 guided to record revenue and margin expansion. CRWV's counterparty capacity was on time and the stock rose 14.9%. The recommendation channel produced nothing in 47 views, so it cannot even be evaluated. (2) Five researchers wrote, without prompting, that taking the run-in apart against peers and the tape was their most useful step and that the playbook does not name it (HSAI, QBTS, RKLB, TTD, LPTH). Separately, P6's positioning sentence is wrong as written: it says a crowded short makes a good print move less. Researchers instead pulled p_up toward 50 for squeeze risk (ASTS, LPTH, FRNM); direction against crowded shorts was 3 of 6, which says positioning is size, not sign. Stage E-P's selected calls on the same names went 5 of 6 (+8.2%, t 1.91), and its sign over all 34 names with a move was 21 of 34. Stage H agreed in sign on all 6 selected names but stayed at 38-58, so the evidence was not missing; the playbook would not let it count. Nothing here rests on returns. The 11-06 day ran without hunt files, so it is cited nowhere. The run-in names that fell (QBTS, HSAI, RKLB, TTD, LPTH, ASTS) mostly exited on one market morning, so they are correlated, and no direction rule is drawn from them.

past_changes_review.predicted: Seed, no formal prediction. It was written to correct the earlier stages' over-pessimism and to make 'priced in' a claim to prove.
past_changes_review.evidence: The priced-in-as-claim part worked as intended: P4 is the most-cited helpful section in approach_notes and kept researchers from shorting visible misses (QBTS, HSAI, RSKD). The over-pessimism did not go away: 0 recommendations in 47 views, p_up confined to 38-58, and Brier skill of 0.003. There are no later revisions to review.

ops.title: How the reaction is decided
ops.text:
A stock trades on the line it trades on: often the guide, the one segment, the one metric the last reactions turned on, not the headline EPS. Find that line first. Read the last reactions and what caused them.

Then take the run-in apart before you read it. Over the last five to twenty sessions, set this stock's move beside its closest peers, its sector basket and the index, and ask which part came with this company's own news and which came with peers' prints or the tape. A move that came with a peer's results or with the market is not evidence about this company. It shifts the bar this release has to clear without saying whether the release clears it. So ask whether this company's own evidence supports the level the peers or the tape took it to. Where it does not, the price is ahead of the evidence, which is as real a gap as a stale estimate; where it does, the move is not a reason to fade it. For a high-beta name, say how large an ordinary overnight or morning move is on market noise alone, and keep p_up about what the release does to the price, not about the tape.

Positioning sets the size more than the direction: a crowded short makes a good print move more and a bad one less; a big run-up makes a good print move less and a bad one more. Put a possible squeeze into `abs_move_pct`, not into a pull toward 50. Remember the window you are scored on (your definition states it): a reaction that needs weeks to play out does not count.
ops.rationale: The researchers kept inventing the same step (peer and tape decomposition of the run-in) and naming its absence as a gap. Putting it in the playbook makes it routine, and makes it say what the decomposition means for p_up: a peer- or tape-driven level is a bar raised without this company's evidence, which is a positioning fact, not a direction. The old positioning sentence was garbled: it lumped a crowded short with a big run-up, and the researchers worked around it by pulling p_up toward 50 for squeeze risk. Positioning direction was 3 of 6 against crowded shorts (ASTS, LPTH, TTD down; CRWV, CAPR, FRNM up), which fits 'size, not sign'. The edit does not prescribe fading rallies. The six run-in names that fell mostly exited on one market morning and are not used as evidence of direction.
ops.predicted_effect: In hp.v2 hunts whose sealed 5-day or 20-day run-up is 8% or more in absolute size, at least 80% carry in `market_holds` an explicit split of the run-in into own news, peers and tape. approach_notes stop naming the decomposition as missing (it was named in 5 of 31 resolved hunt files under hp.v1). questions_pursued no longer record moves toward 50 justified only by squeeze risk. On paired names, hp.v2's Brier is no worse than the control's.
ops.revert_if: Two outcomes would show this was wrong. First, over at least 30 resolved hp.v2 names, the names whose hunt attributes most of the run-in to peers or the tape score a worse paired Brier than the control on the same names (mean difference above +0.01). Second, the decomposition is absent from most qualifying hunts, so the text changed nothing and should be removed.

ops.title: Calibration and when to recommend
ops.text:
`p_up` is your honest probability that the stock is higher at the end of the window. 50 means you cannot tell. Move away from 50 only as far as the evidence takes you.

The line a print turns on (the next-period guide, the margin, bookings) is almost never visible before the release. That is the normal case and not, by itself, a reason to stay at 50. What you can see are its inputs: the company's record of guiding against what it then reported, counterparties' and peers' disclosures since it last spoke, your own arithmetic of what the line needs, and what consensus and the price assume about it. Estimate which way the line is likely to land against what the price holds, and let that estimate set p_up. Not being able to see the line is not the same as having shown that the price holds it (P8).

Recommend (`action` long or short) only when all three hold:
- your probability that the direction is right is 65 or more;
- you can name the mechanism: the dated evidence that makes one side of the deciding line more likely than the price assumes, the reason the price does not hold it, and why this release will show it inside the window;
- your strongest case against it (`self_critique`) does not change your mind.

There is no quota. Zero recommendations on a day is fine; so are several.
ops.rationale: As read by the researchers, the old mechanism clause asked for the release's content to be seen before the release, a condition no print can meet. On seven resolved names the researcher found dated evidence on the inputs to the deciding line and then explicitly declined to let it move p_up because the line itself 'has no public trace before the release' (QBTS, HSAI, CRWV, RKLB, STUB, HIMS, LQDA). After the fact the inputs were often right on the facts: RKLB beat and guided up with margin expansion, as its guiding record suggested, and CRWV's counterparty capacity was on time before the stock rose 14.9%. The result was 0 recommendations in 47 views and only 3 of 35 p_up values 10 or more points from 50. The edit keeps the 65 bar and the three conditions, and changes only what the mechanism must show: evidence that one side of the line is more likely than the price assumes, not sight of the line. It rests on the reasoning failure, not on returns.
ops.predicted_effect: p_up spreads out: the share of hp.v2 views with |p_up - 50| of 10 or more rises from 3/35 (9%) to at least 20%. At least 3 recommendations appear over the first 30 resolved hp.v2 names, against 0 under hp.v1. approach_notes stop citing an unobservable deciding line as the reason to stop. Brier skill against a coin on hp.v2 rises above the control's on the paired names.
ops.revert_if: Three outcomes would show this was wrong. First, over at least 30 resolved hp.v2 names, the paired Brier against the control is worse (mean difference above +0.01 with t above 1), or hp.v2's Brier skill against a coin falls below 0. Second, the drift alarm fires. Third, once 10 or more recommendations have resolved, fewer than half are right.
